openings.label: Greek Black Sea colonization begins
openings.note: Ionian Greek settlers found Olbia, Chersonesus, and other cities on the northern Black Sea coast — the earliest settlements in today's Ukraine this catalog documents, roughly 1,500 years before Kyivan Rusʹ.

openings.label: Kyivan Rusʹ founded
openings.note: Oleg unites Novgorod and Kyiv; the first East Slavic state centered on Kyiv.

openings.label: Mongol sack of Kyiv
openings.note: Kyivan Rusʹ fragments; Galicia-Volhynia becomes the leading Rusʹ successor state.

openings.label: Poland annexes Galicia
openings.note: Casimir III takes the Kingdom of Galicia-Volhynia; other Rusʹ lands pass to Lithuania over the following decades.

openings.label: Union of Lublin
openings.note: Lithuania cedes most Ukrainian lands to the Polish Crown, forming the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.

openings.label: Khmelnytsky Uprising / Pereiaslav (1654)
openings.note: The Cossack Hetmanate emerges as an autonomous state in 1648, then accepts Russian protection at Pereiaslav in 1654 — a foundational, still-contested moment in Russo-Ukrainian history.

openings.label: Partitions of Poland begin
openings.note: By 1795, Russia annexes most Ukrainian lands; Austria annexes Galicia.

openings.label: Peace of Riga
openings.note: Ends the war of independence: Galicia and Volhynia to Poland, the rest becomes Soviet Ukraine.

openings.label: WWII annexations
openings.note: The USSR absorbs eastern Poland (1939), then Bukovina/Bessarabia and Transcarpathia by 1945.

openings.label: Independence
openings.note: Ukraine declares independence as the USSR dissolves.

openings.label: Crimea annexed / Donbas war
openings.note: Russia annexes Crimea; war begins in eastern Ukraine.

openings.label: Full-scale invasion
openings.note: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
